title: Performance & Indexing
tagline: join algorithms, index tuning, statistics, query optimization

placementQuiz.q: Nested Loop Join is best when:
options: One table is small, other has index on join key
placementQuiz.explain: NLJ: for each outer row, probe inner index. Best when outer is small and inner has index.

placementQuiz.q: Hash Join builds hash table on:
placementQuiz.explain: Hash Join: build hash on smaller (build) table, probe with larger. Memory-intensive.

options: Both tables sorted on join key
placementQuiz.explain: Merge Join: both inputs sorted on join key, then merged like merge sort. O(N+M).
work_mem controls memory for sorts, hashes, and materialization. Spills to disk if exceeded.
ANALYZE collects table statistics (n_distinct, most_common_vals, histograms) for planner.

sections.title: Join Algorithms — How the Planner Joins

blocks.md: Planner picks algorithm: Nested Loop (small + index), Hash Join (large, no index), Merge Join (pre-sorted). EXPLAIN shows which. You can influence with indexes, stats, enable_* settings.

blocks.label: join algorithms in EXPLAIN
blocks.mysql:
-- MySQL: primarily Nested Loop
-- Hash Join: 8.0.18+ (hash_join optimizer hint)
-- Merge Join: not directly controllable
blocks.py-pandas:
# No planner, but merge = merge sort join:
pd.merge(a, b, on='key', how='inner', sort=True)  # uses sort-merge

blocks.md: **Hash Join:** Build side (5000 rows) → hash table in memory. Probe side (10000 rows) → hash probe. If hash table > work_mem → spills to disk (slow). Increase work_mem for big joins.

items.q: Hash Join spills to disk when:
items.explain: work_mem controls hash table memory. Spill = massive slowdown. Increase work_mem or use indexes.

options: Tables already sorted on join key
Both tables have ORDER BY on join key
items.explain: Merge Join requires sorted input. Index scan or explicit sort provides ordering.

blocks.md: Planner uses: histogram (most common values), n_distinct, null_frac, correlation. For range: histogram bounds + linear interpolation. For equality: MCV list + 1/n_distinct for non-MCV. For correlated columns: independence assumption (wrong) unless extended stats exist.

blocks.title: Bitmap Index Scan — Multiple Indexes Combined

blocks.md: **Bitmap Index Scan:** Combines multiple indexes in memory (bitmap), then single heap fetch. Great for AND/OR combinations where no composite index exists. Recheck Cond means heap tuple rechecked (lossy pages).

items.q: Bitmap Index Scan is chosen when:
options: Multiple indexes can be combined for AND/OR
items.explain: BitmapAnd/BitmapOr combines multiple index scans in memory before heap access.

items.q: "Recheck Cond" in Bitmap Heap Scan means:
options: Heap tuple rechecked due to lossy bitmap pages
items.explain: Lossy bitmap pages store page-level not tuple-level. Must recheck each tuple.

blocks.text: Partial Indexes — Index Only What You Query

blocks.label: partial index
blocks.pg:
-- Partial index (PostgreSQL native)
CREATE INDEX idx ON t (col) WHERE status = 'active';
blocks.mysql:
-- MySQL: no native partial index
-- Workaround: partitioned table or generated column
blocks.py-pandas:
# Filter first, then operate
active = employees[employees['status'] == 'active']
# Then operate on smaller DataFrame

blocks.label: expression indexes & collation
blocks.py-pandas:
# Pre-compute expressions
df['full_name'] = df['first_name'] + ' ' + df['last_name']
events['year_month'] = events['created_at'].dt.to_period('M')

blocks.md: **Expression must be IMMUTABLE.** No NOW(), random(), volatile functions. Expression index stores computed value — if function isn't immutable, index becomes inconsistent.

items.q: Partial index WHERE status='active' helps query:
items.explain: Partial index only contains 'active' rows. Predicate must include status='active' to match.
Expression must match exactly. Index on (salary * 12) helps WHERE salary * 12 > 600000.

revisionCard: Nested Loop: small outer + indexed inner; Hash: large both, build hash on smaller; Merge: pre-sorted
Composite index: equality first, then range; (a,b) works for a=1 and a=1,b=2
Partial index: WHERE clause on index — smaller, faster for skewed access
Covering index (INCLUDE): index-only scan, avoids heap fetch
Sargable: column naked on left, constant on right. No functions/math/casts on column
Bitmap Index Scan: combines multiple indexes in memory; Recheck Cond = lossy pages

glossary.def: For each outer row, probe inner index. Best: small outer + indexed inner.
Build hash table on smaller input, probe with larger. Memory-heavy; spills to disk if > work_mem.
Both inputs sorted on join key; linear merge. O(N+M). Requires sorted input.
Index with WHERE clause — only indexes subset of rows matching condition.
Index with INCLUDE columns — satisfies query without heap lookup.
Search ARGument ABLE — predicate that can use index seek (e.g., col = 5).
